families.s: HSE inerting of enclosed process plant
families.t: nitrogen, carbon dioxide, argon, oxygen control, tanks, reactors, liquid transfer, asphyxiation and permit to work
f: Replacing air or a flammable atmosphere with inert gas is an effective explosion-prevention method.
Inerting is normally considered after eliminating or reducing the flammable hazard by simpler means.
Typical applications include storage tanks and reactor systems.
Inert gas may also be used to transfer flammable liquids under pressure.
Inerting is effective mainly in enclosed plant where oxygen concentration can be controlled.
Nitrogen, carbon dioxide, argon, helium and suitable flue gases can be used.
Inert atmospheres create an asphyxiation hazard, especially in confined spaces.
Entry into inerted equipment requires formal controls such as permit-to-work and atmosphere verification.

families.s: HSE inspection and non-destructive testing management
families.t: written schemes, technique selection, competence, limitations, defect evaluation, records, follow-up and continued safe operation
f: NDT supports assessment of plant condition without necessarily damaging the equipment.
NDT should form part of an organised inspection and integrity-management process.
Written schemes of examination may define equipment, examination scope and intervals.
The selected technique should be capable of detecting the expected defect type and location.
Dutyholders should understand the capabilities and limitations of each NDT method.
Competent personnel should specify, perform and interpret examinations.
Results should be evaluated and used to determine repair, monitoring or continued-operation decisions.
NDT records and follow-up actions should support the demonstrated continued safe operation of plant.

families.t: detector objectives, detector type, positioning, dispersion, alarms, maintenance, management and human factors
f: Leak and gas detection can identify unplanned releases and support containment control.
Detection objectives should be defined before detector technology is selected.
Detector type should match the substance, environment and required duty.
Positioning should reflect credible leak sources, gas behaviour, dispersion and dilution.
Wrong detector types or poor locations can create ineffective protection.
Detection systems should communicate alarms or initiate appropriate control actions.
Detectors require calibration, testing and maintenance.
Management should avoid excessive reliance on detection where prevention and containment are reasonably practicable.

families.s: HSE maintenance procedures for safety-critical plant
families.t: planned maintenance, risk based maintenance, proof testing, competence, communication, faults, isolation and return to service
f: Maintenance procedures are necessary to prevent and mitigate major accidents.
Lack of maintenance can cause failure of safety-critical equipment.
Human error during maintenance can introduce new hazards.
Maintenance regimes may be planned, risk based, reliability centred, condition based or breakdown based.
The selected regime should be adequate for every item with a safety function.
Proof-test intervals should keep safety-critical risk within acceptable limits.
Maintenance staff need appropriate competence, information and supervision.
Isolation, permit control, communication and formal return to service should be included where relevant.

families.s: HSE operating procedures for process plant
families.t: normal operation, abnormal operation, temporary procedures, start-up, shutdown, commissioning, emergency procedures and validation
f: Clear, concise and accurate operating procedures are an important control against major accidents.
Procedures should reflect actual plant practice and plant practice should follow the procedures.
Written procedures should cover normal, abnormal, temporary and emergency operation.
Commissioning, start-up, shutdown, loading, unloading and process change require defined instructions.
Procedures should identify roles, plant condition, controls, PPE and key process parameters.
Changes to equipment, chemicals, tasks or personnel should trigger controlled review.
Safety-critical procedures should be based on task analysis and should be accessible to users.
Procedures should be formally validated before issue and kept current through document control.
